revisions.title: Completeness as the lawgiver’s test
revisions.body: What makes this passage memorable is the Athenian’s test of completeness. The Sauromatian example names women sharing horses, bows, and other weapons with men; it does not itself describe military training. The Athenian turns that case into a feasibility argument, then compares Thracian, local, and Laconian arrangements. I read the sequence as a challenge to ask not merely what is customary, but how fully a city lets women share civic practices.
